items.stem: Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines due to a straight current carrying conductor indicating the direction of current in the conductor and the direction of the corresponding magnetic field lines.
items.answer: The magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor are concentric circles centred on the conductor and lying in planes perpendicular to it. Their direction is given by the right-hand thumb rule : if the conductor is held in the right hand with the extended thumb pointing along the direction of the current, the curled fingers give the direction of the magnetic field lines. Closer to the wire the circles are crowded (stronger field) and they get farther apart as the distance from the wire increases.

items.stem: Why does a freely suspended magnet always point in the geographic north-south direction ?
items.answer: The earth has a magnetic field around it. It behaves as if a huge bar magnet is placed at its centre. The north pole of this huge bar magnet lies towards the geographic south pole of the earth, and the south pole of this bar magnet lies towards the geographic north pole of the earth. When a magnet is suspended freely at the surface of the earth, its north pole moves towards the magnetic south pole of the earth's magnet, i.e. the geographic north pole of the earth, and its south pole moves towards the magnetic north pole of the earth's magnet, i.e. the geographic south pole of the earth.

items.stem: Write the properties of a bar magnet.
items.answer: (i) A bar magnet attracts small pieces of magnetic substances like iron, cobalt and nickel. The attraction is maximum at the free ends; these ends are called poles. (ii) If a bar magnet is suspended freely in a horizontal plane, it takes the north-south direction. The end which points towards the north is called the north pole and the end which points towards the south is called the south pole. (iii) Like poles repel and unlike poles attract each other. (iv) If we break a magnet into two or more smaller pieces, even the smallest possible magnet has both north and south poles.

items.stem: What are permanent magnet and electromagnet ? Give two uses of each.
items.answer: Those magnets which have constant magnetic fields around them are called permanent magnets. When a soft iron is placed inside a solenoid and current is passed through it, the soft iron gets magnetised; the magnet so formed is called an electromagnet. Uses : a permanent magnet is used in (i) an electric generator and (ii) a loudspeaker; an electromagnet is used in (i) cranes and (ii) an electric bell.

items.stem: What is meant by the magnetic field lines ? List any two properties of magnetic field lines.
items.answer: (a) The lines drawn in a magnetic field along which a north pole would move are called magnetic field lines. (b) Properties : (i) The magnetic field lines originate from the north pole and merge at the south pole outside the magnet, and go from south to north inside the magnet. (ii) No two magnetic field lines intersect each other.

items.answer: The current carrying conductor should be placed in the plane of the paper itself. The axis of the compass is vertical and the field due to the conductor is also vertical. items.stem: What is a solenoid ? Draw a diagram to show the magnetic field lines around a solenoid. What is its main use ?
items.answer: A solenoid is a long coil containing a large number of close turns of insulated copper wire. The magnetic field lines around a current-carrying solenoid are like those of a bar magnet - uniform and parallel inside the solenoid, and looping round from one end to the other outside it. A solenoid is used to magnetise any magnetic material.

items.stem: State Fleming's left hand rule. A positively charged particle projected towards west is deflected towards north by a magnetic field. Find the direction of magnetic field.
items.answer: According to Fleming's left-hand rule, let the thumb, forefinger and central finger of the left hand be stretched so that they are mutually perpendicular to one another. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the central finger points in the direction of the current, the thumb gives the direction of the force acting on the conductor. items.stem: What do you understand by live and neutral wires ? Do both of them carry high voltage ?
items.answer: The electric power line which enters our houses contains two wires. The wire having high potential is called the live wire. The other wire, which is maintained at zero potential by connecting it to the earth at the power station, is called the neutral wire. So both do not carry high voltage - only the live wire does. The potential difference between these two lines is 220 volts in India.

items.stem: Name two safety measures commonly used in electric circuits and appliances. What precautions should be taken while using them ?
items.answer: The two safety measures commonly used are (i) the electric fuse and (ii) earthing of the metallic body of the appliance. Precautions : the fuse must be of the correct current rating and must be connected in series in the live wire; the earth wire must be properly connected to the metal case of every appliance; damaged plugs, switches and sockets should be replaced at once and never touched with wet hands.

items.stem: Why do we use a thin wire as a fuse wire ?
items.answer: We use a thin wire as a fuse wire because it has a higher resistance as compared to the other connecting wires. As a result, the heating effect of the current is much more in the fuse wire, due to which it melts easily and protects the electrical appliance.

items.stem: What is an electric fuse ?
items.answer: An electric fuse is a piece of wire of a material having a very low melting point and high resistance. When a high current flows through the circuit due to short circuiting or overloading, the fuse wire gets heated and melts. It is a safety device.

items.stem:
Explain what is short circuiting and overloading in an electric supply.
Or
Write difference between over-loading and short circuiting.
items.answer: (a) An electric circuit is said to be short circuited if the live wire and the neutral wire come in contact with each other. (b) Overloading means connecting too many power appliances to a single socket or drawing more current than the circuit is designed for.
items.ocr: Printed part (b) is garbled ('Overloading means to connect to power appliances with single socket and vault device in electrical circuit'); rewritten in its plain sense.

items.stem: Why is a spark produced at the place of short circuit ? Why is the spark of white colour ?
items.answer: When short circuiting occurs, the resistance of the circuit decreases to a very small value. As a result, a sudden flow of very large current takes place. This heats up the live wire and vaporises the metal, which causes the spark. The metal of the wire becomes very hot, and very hot objects emit white light. That is why the spark appears white.

items.stem: (i) Two magnetic field lines do not intersect each other. Why ? (ii) How is a uniform magnetic field in a given region represented ? Draw a diagram in support of your answer.
items.answer: (i) If two field lines intersected each other, then at the point of intersection two tangents, and hence two directions of the magnetic field, could be drawn. This is not possible, because at any one point the magnetic field can have only one direction. (ii) A uniform magnetic field in a region is represented by parallel and equidistant field lines.

items.stem: Study the diagram given below and answer the questions that follow : (a) Why do the iron filings arrange in such a pattern ? (b) What does this pattern demonstrate ? (c) Why do the iron filings near the bar magnet seem to align in the shape of closed curves ?
items.answer: (a) The iron filings arrange themselves in a pattern because they get attracted by the bar magnet and turn along the field; the pattern they form traces the magnetic field lines of the bar magnet. (b) The pattern demonstrates that the magnetic field is strongest at the poles of the magnet and becomes weaker as we go farther from the magnet. The magnetic field lines emerge from the north pole of the magnet and end at its south pole. (c) The iron filings arrange themselves in closed loops around a bar magnet because magnetic field lines are closed curves.

items.stem: (i) What is the function of earth wire in electrical instruments ? (ii) Explain what is short circuiting an electric supply. (iii) What is the usual current rating of the fuse wire in the line to feed (a) lights and fans ? (b) appliances of 2 kW or more power ?
items.answer: (i) The earth wire is a safety device used in electric circuits. At the time of leakage of current, most of the electric current goes into the earth, so we are protected from electric shocks and the appliance is not damaged. (ii) When, accidentally, the live wire and the neutral wire of an electric circuit come into direct contact, it is called short circuiting. A very large quantity of electric current then flows through the circuit. (iii) (a) 5 A. (b) 15 A.

items.stem: You are given two identical looking iron bars. Just using these two bars how will you identify whether any or both of these bars is/are a magnet ?
items.answer: Repeatedly tap one of the bars. If it is the iron bar, nothing much will change. If it is the magnet, it will demagnetise a bit, reducing the force between the two bars. If you get no effect after many taps, you can switch to tapping the other bar, to make sure that you get some effect one way or the other.

items.stem: Demonstrate that due to motion of a magnet near a solenoid coil an induced current is set up in the coil.
items.answer: Take a solenoid coil of insulated copper wire AB having a number of turns (about 20 or more). Connect the ends of the coil to a sensitive galvanometer. Now take a bar magnet NS and rapidly bring the magnet towards the end B of the coil. The galvanometer suddenly gives a momentary deflection in one direction. Now take the magnet away from the coil; the galvanometer again gives a momentary deflection, but in the opposite direction. Now fix the magnet in one position so that it is stationary with respect to the coil - there is no deflection in the galvanometer. Again keep the magnet fixed and gently move the coil AB either towards or away from the magnet; we get a deflection in the galvanometer even now. Thus it is proved that an induced current is produced whenever there is relative motion between the coil and the magnet.

items.stem: State different ways to induce current in coil.
items.answer: (i) The current can be induced in a coil by rotating it in the magnetic field between the poles of a U-shaped magnet. (ii) The current can be induced in a coil by keeping it stationary and rotating a magnet inside it. (iii) The current can be induced in a coil by changing the current continuously in another coil kept near it.

items.stem: (a) Give the significance of the following in a domestic circuit : (i) electric meter, (ii) earthing. (b) List two precautions that should be taken to avoid overloading.
items.answer: (a) (i) Electric meter : it is used to record the consumption of electrical energy in kWh in the circuit. (ii) Earthing : it prevents electric shock. The earth wire is joined to the metal case of the appliance and provides a low resistance conducting path for the current. (b) (i) Too many appliances should not be connected to a single socket. (ii) Fuses of current rating 5 A and 15 A should be used separately in the domestic circuit.

items.stem: Explain two ways to induce current in a coil. When is the induced current produced highest ? State the rule used to find direction of induced current.
items.answer: (i) By moving a magnet towards or away from a coil. (ii) By varying the current in one coil, an induced emf is produced in a nearby coil. The induced current is highest when the direction of motion of the coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field. Fleming's right-hand rule is used to find the direction of the induced current : if we stretch the thumb, the first finger and the central finger of the right hand mutually perpendicular to each other, and the first finger points along the direction of the field while the thumb indicates the direction of motion of the conductor, then the central finger gives the direction of the induced current.

items.stem: Write some precautions in the use of electricity.
items.answer: (a) Damaged plugs, switches, sockets, etc. should be replaced immediately. (b) Plugs, switches or sockets should not be touched with wet hands. (c) All electrical appliances should be given earth connections. (d) All the connections and joints at different switches and plugs must be tight to avoid sparking. (e) Rubber gloves and rubber shoes should be worn while handling a live circuit. (f) The main circuit should be switched off if there is any sparking or fire in the circuit. (g) Water should not be thrown in case of fire due to an electric short circuit.
